newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge CEO sees strong nickel demand.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge CEO sees strong nickel demand.

text.p: Falconbridge Ltd Chief Executive Oyvind Hushovd said on Friday that demand for nickel was strong and supplies were expected to remain tight in the near term.
Meanwhile, demand for copper was expected to remain strong with firm prices during at least the first half of 1997.

"Growth trends for these two metals are outpacing the world economy," Hushovd told shareholders at the annual meeting. Stainless steel, which accounts for two-thirds of nickel consumption, was expected to continue its long-term growth rate of 5.3 percent per year for the years ahead.

Other nickel markets, including alloys for the aerospace sector, were expected to see strong growth. Long-term growth rates for global nickel consumption were forecast to be 4.1 percent, Hushovd said.
"Our short-term forecast for the nickel market is that supplies of nickel will remain constrained by existing capacity and stocks will drop accordingly," he said.

Hushovd said 1998 production from Falconbridge's C$500 million Raglan project in Quebec would not be sufficient to balance supply and demand. He said Raglan was on schedule to begin concentrate production this December.
Falconbridge estimated Raglan's cash operating costs would be under US$1.50 per pound.
In the medium term, Falconbridge forecast nickel inventories will decline to the equivalent of 6.6 weeks of consumption in 1997, from eight weeks of consumption at the end of 1996.
Inventories are expected to drop further to a tight six weeks for 1998 and 1999, Hushovd said.
The strong growth rate in western world copper demand is projected to continue through the end of this decade. Copper demand has grown at an annual rate of 3.5 percent since 1985.
"However, new production from Chile, Indonesia and Peru will increase supply at the rate of four to five percent per year over the balance of the decade," Hushovd said.
"We therefore expect the copper price to come under increasing pressure over the medium term as a result of this supply and demand imbalance," he added.

But in the short term, Falconbridge sees a very tight supply situation with metal inventories at minimal levels. "Demand is projected to remain strong leading us to expect firm copper prices during at least the first half of this year," Hushovd said.
Falconbridge said full commercial production at the Collahuasi copper property in Chile is on target for January 1, 1999.
Collahuasi's solvent extraction - electro winning plant is expected to be commissioned in April of 1998. The concentrator should start up in August of the same year.
Falconbridge expects operating costs will be below US$0.45 per pound once Collahuasi is in full production.
